info.title: Mipyme API
info.description:
Mipyme helps retail and service businesses manage products, customers, suppliers, purchases, and sales under one merchant account.

## Conventions
Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Your account controls merchant and location access; health is public. Requests and responses use JSON except realtime authorization (form fields). `/v1` uses `snake_case`; send money as decimal strings.
Lists use cursor pagination: omit `cursor` on the first page, then send `next_cursor` with unchanged filters while `has_more` is true. PATCH updates supplied fields only; omit fields to preserve them or use `null` to clear when allowed.

## Retries and errors
POST endpoints documenting `Idempotency-Key` support retries. Errors include `code`, `message`, HTTP `status`, `request_id`, and `details`. Handle by `code`; keep `request_id` for investigation.

tags.description: Invitations let a person join a business as an employee by linking their login to it.

tags.description: Realtime notifications report changes to your merchant's data. Authorize the private channel for your merchant before subscribing.

tags.description: Use the current account endpoint to identify the account associated with your access token.

tags.name: Onboarding
tags.description: Onboarding associates an owner account with a merchant and its first location. Staff accounts cannot create a merchant.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Products are the goods and services in a merchant's catalog. Use collections to group related products and variants to define the options available for sale.

tags.name: Collections
tags.description: Collections group related products in a merchant's catalog. Each product can belong to one collection.

tags.name: Suppliers
tags.description: Suppliers provide products to a merchant. Link them to purchases to track where received stock came from.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Customers are the people or businesses who buy from a merchant. Link a customer to a sale to record who made the purchase.

tags.name: Sales
tags.description: A sale records a checkout at a location. Review its fulfillment and payment history, or void a fulfilled sale to restore item quantities.

tags.name: Purchases
tags.description: A purchase records stock received from a supplier at a location. Use it to track where inventory came from and what it cost.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Download a full or incremental snapshot of merchant resources for offline use.

post.description: Downloads the merchant, products, collections, customers, suppliers, and all merchant locations in one unpaginated response. Requires enabled merchant membership. Send "*" for full sync, then the returned token for incremental sync. Incremental queries use updated_at between the previous checkpoint minus one hour and the current checkpoint, inclusively. The overlap can replay recent records and covers delayed commits within that window; it cannot guarantee delivery of transactions that commit after falling outside the overlap. Products are returned complete when their own or related record timestamps qualify, including archived products. All reads share one consistent database snapshot. Redis stores the checkpoint timestamp for 30 days. Authentic expired tokens or missing checkpoints trigger full sync; malformed, tampered, and wrong-merchant tokens are rejected. Successful requests issue fresh merchant-bound tokens with no device identity; older tokens retain their original expiry. Save each token atomically with the applied response. The new checkpoint is saved only after all resource queries succeed. Database failures return 500 and Redis failures return 503, without a new token. No resource selection, deletion tracking, pagination, or record or byte cap.

200.description: Returns complete qualifying resources and a new sync token. Empty arrays indicate no eligible records. merchant is null when no merchant update qualifies. Recent records can be replayed by the one-hour overlap.

400.description: The request contains invalid JSON or values, or the token is malformed, tampered, or belongs to another merchant. Returns validation_error or sync_token_invalid.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired. Returns invalid_oauth_token.

403.description: The account has no provisioned membership, or its employee is disabled or archived. Returns account_not_provisioned or forbidden_error.

500.description: A database or resource-query failure prevented sync. No new token is issued. Returns internal_server_error.

503.description: Redis cannot read or save the checkpoint. Retry with the same token. Returns sync_unavailable.

post.summary: Invite an employee to create an account
post.description: Emails the employee an invitation to create a personal account. Signing in with that email and accepting the invitation links the login to the employee. Invitations expire after 7 days; sending a new one revokes the pending one, which is how you resend it. Requires the owner or `manage_employees`. The owner, employees with an account, and archived employees cannot be invited. In staging and production the email is sent after the response, in English for Belize and in Spanish elsewhere; a delivery failure does not fail the request.

post.description: Creates a product and its initial variant. Items start as drafts, require positive `unit_cost`, and get an inventory level at every location of your merchant. Use `inventory_levels` to set opening stock and stock thresholds per location; opening stock is recorded as an `initial_stock` movement. Services start active, do not track inventory, and ignore `inventory_levels`. Requires an enabled owner or staff member.

201.description: Returns the created product and its default variant. Items start as draft; services start as active.

400.description: The request contains invalid JSON or invalid field values, an item is missing unit_cost or has zero unit_cost, an item's price is below its unit_cost, `inventory_levels` repeats a location, or a `low_stock_threshold` is not lower than a positive `optimal_stock_level`. Returns `price_below_unit_cost` when the price is below the unit cost and `validation_error` otherwise.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired. Returns invalid_oauth_token.

403.description: The account has no provisioned membership (account_not_provisioned), its employee is disabled or archived, or the `created_by_id` employee is not enabled (forbidden_error).

500.description: An unexpected error prevented the product from being created. Returns `internal_server_error`.

patch.description: Updates supplied fields; omitted fields are unchanged. Use `null` to clear `sku`, `barcode`, `collection_id`, or `image_url`. For items, `unit_cost` must be positive and may change only before stock moves; `price` cannot be below `unit_cost`. `inventory_levels` changes only the listed locations: thresholds can change at any time, while `on_hand` sets opening stock, recorded as an `initial_stock` movement, and is accepted only before the product's first inventory movement at any location. Services ignore `inventory_levels`.

parameters.description: The product identifier.

Returns `price_below_unit_cost` when the price is below the unit cost and `validation_error` otherwise.

line_items.description: The products received in the delivery, with costs, prices, and quantities grouped by variant.

notes.description: The staff notes associated with the delivery. Returns `null` if no notes are recorded.

name.description: The display name of the employee.

created_by.description: The employee who recorded the delivery. Returns `null` if no employee is associated.

created_at.description: The date and time when the purchase order was created, in RFC 3339 format.

updated_at.description: The date and time when the purchase order was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

void_reason.description: The reason recorded when the purchase was voided, with surrounding whitespace removed. Returns `null` when no reason was supplied.

name.description: The display name of the employee.

voided_by.description: The employee associated with voiding the purchase. Returns `null` if no voiding employee is recorded.

voided_at.description: The time when the purchase was voided, in RFC 3339 format. Returns `null` until the purchase is voided.

Purchase.description: A record of products received from a supplier at a location. It preserves the quantities and costs recorded for each variant.

results.description: The purchases returned in this page.

next_cursor.description: The opaque cursor to pass when requesting the next page. Returns `null` on the final page.

has_more.description: Whether more purchases are available after this page.

SalePaginationResponse.description: A page of sales with the information needed to request the next page.

results.description: The sales returned in this page.

next_cursor.description: The opaque cursor to pass when requesting the next page. Returns `null` on the final page.

has_more.description: Whether more sales are available after this page.

reason.description: An optional reason for voiding the purchase, up to 256 characters after surrounding whitespace is removed. Omitted, blank, or `null` values return as `null`.

voided_by_id.description: The employee credited with voiding the purchase, such as whoever unlocked a shared device with their PIN. Must be an enabled employee of your merchant. VoidPurchaseRequest.description: Optional reason for voiding a purchase.

bearerAuth.description: A bearer access token issued by the configured identity provider. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Use a UUID v4 or opaque key (max 255 characters) for POST retries. Keys are scoped to the authenticated user across POST endpoints; do not include sensitive data.

Reuse the key with the same path, query values, and JSON body. Match JSON field/array order, repeated query-value order, and types; whitespace and query-parameter order may differ. Original status and response are replayed except for `validation_error`, which can be corrected and retried with the same key. Different requests return `idempotency_key_mismatch`.

Keys expire 24 hours after the first valid request. In-progress retries may return `idempotency_request_in_progress`; verify the outcome before using another key. Expired keys may execute again. Retries require authentication, permissions, and rate limits.
